title: The Nazarene sect, sacrifice and flesh — prep board
subtitle: Internal. How to hold the resolution, what Huff, Boyce and Jones actually said, the six holes, and the do-not-say list.

it: 3 · CLAIM A · NO FLESH (THE MOVEMENT AFTER HIM)
4 · CLAIM B · THE STREAM, NOT A MEMBERSHIP CARD
REV. TONY JONES WILL SAY (he had the apparatus)
THE HOLES · 5 IS NEW AND IS THE WORST
★★ STRONGER ARGUMENTS · FOUND IN KAM'S 12 APPEARANCES, 2026-10-16
AND THE HARD NEWS FROM THE SAME 22 HOURS
WE HOLD THESE · NOBODY USED THEM

THE RESOLUTION

"The historical Jesus belonged to a Nazarene sect that rejected sacrifice and flesh consumption."

Read the sentence carefully. The relative clause attaches to THE SECT, not to Jesus. It is not one claim, it is two, and they are not equally strong. Keep them apart all night and you can lose B without losing A.

CLAIM A — the sect rejected sacrifice and abstained from flesh.
CLAIM B — Jesus belonged to that sect.

A is where the evidence is. B is where the fight will be.

If you merge them, every hit on B reads as a hit on A. Say out loud, early: "These are two claims. Let me give you the evidence for each separately."

CONCEDE THESE IN THE FIRST TWO MINUTES

1. No ancient source says "Jesus was an Essene." Not one. The word essene does not even occur in the Dead Sea Scrolls.

2. Luke 24:42-43 says the risen Jesus ate fish. Textually secure — P75, Sinaiticus, Vaticanus. Only the honeycomb is a variant. Do NOT call the verse unstable.

3. The Essene/Ebionite identification is not a scholarly consensus and we are not claiming it definitively.

Conceding these costs nothing and buys the room. Refusing to concede them is how this argument has actually been lost on camera.

CLAIM IT AS A STREAM, NOT A MEMBERSHIP CARD.

A vocabulary found nowhere in the Hebrew Bible — "spirit of truth", "children of light" — runs all through the gospels. Same proof text, same wilderness, same immersion.

That is a stream. It is not a membership roll, and you do not need one: he ate with sinners and drank wine, and reform movements criticise their parent hardest.

THIS HALF IS RED TEXT ABOUT JESUS HIMSELF.

He threw Hosea 6:6 at the men running the cult — twice. He stopped the Temple traffic quoting the one chapter where God denies commanding burnt offerings. And the next verse says that is the moment they decided to kill him:

Mark 11:18 (KJV) — "And the scribes and chief priests heard it, and sought how they might destroy him."

Nothing else on this board is this strong. Lead here.

WHY THIS SECTION HOLDS: every witness in it was hostile or disinterested.

Paul concedes vegetable-only believers in Rome by 57 CE — against his own argument. Epiphanius is trying to discredit them. A church council legislates against what is actually happening.

Nobody in this list wanted the conclusion. That is what makes it evidence.

Concede the asymmetry out loud: this is evidence about THE MOVEMENT, not about what was on Jesus's plate.

THE STRONGEST SINGLE MOVE ON THIS BOARD

Matthew 19:8 — "Moses because of the hardness of your hearts suffered you to put away your wives: but from the beginning it was not so."

Jesus, in the red text, identifies a standing Torah permission as a CONCESSION to hardness of heart, and appeals past it to the beginning. That is the whole hermeneutic, in his own mouth, applied by him to a different question.

It answers "Genesis 9:3 permits meat" without denying that it permits meat. Permission is not endorsement — and he is the one who says so.

It is also the canonical twin of Recognitions 1.36, whose chapter title is literally "Allowance of Sacrifice for a Time". The card calls that our biggest unexploited asset; this gives it a gospel parallel.

Kam used this against Rev. Tony Jones (@ 145:40) and against the carnivore (@ 51:04). Jones never answered it. Neither did Hicks.

Recognitions 1.36 is titled "Allowance of Sacrifice for a Time."

The Jewish-Christian text says the sacrifices were a temporary concession to a people who had learned the habit in Egypt — not a divine requirement.

Pair it with Matthew 19:8 and you have the same logic in the red text and in the movement that claimed succession from him.

BOYCE WILL SAY: "The church fathers you cite condemn you."
(Huff/Boyce debate @ 126:00, 131:46, 134:15)

Jerome and Epiphanius explicitly say the Ebionites OF THEIR DAY are not the group Paul collected for in Galatians 2:10. So the witnesses we use for continuity are testifying against continuity.

This is sharper than the usual "they were heretics" version, and the card does not yet answer this form. Answer: their verdict is theological; their REPORTAGE is what we use, and hostile reportage is the strongest kind. Epiphanius had no motive to invent an anti-sacrifice sect.

HUFF WILL SAY: "Your ebion chain is a back-translation, and an argument from silence."
(@ 103:53, 104:17, 105:49)

"None of the Greek passages use ebionim as poor — I'm seeing ptochos. There is no Hebrew Matthew. We have no manuscripts of Matthew other than Greek."

OPEN. The repo has no lexical heading on this and essene-nazarene-origins §1 never addresses the Hebrew-to-Greek step. Do not improvise it.

HUFF WILL SAY: "There was sacrifice at Qumran — read Liane Feldman at NYU."
(@ 128:15)

The ARCHAEOLOGICAL form of the objection. Our cards answer only the TEXTUAL form (Temple Scroll, 4QMMT). Feldman appears nowhere in the repo.

Safe answer tonight: concede we are arguing from the texts, and that the archaeology is contested. Do not pretend to have read her.

HUFF WILL SAY: "Jesus taught in Greek, and Hebrew was functionally a dead liturgical language."
(@ 106:32, 111:40; cites Stanley Porter 1993, Peter J. Williams)

Matthew 5 alliterates in Greek and jumbles when back-translated; Galilee was a koine trade region; John 12:20-22 has Greeks approaching Philip.

OPEN. The repo has nothing on the language of Jesus's teaching, and this undercuts the whole Hebrew-substratum move at the root.

HUFF WILL SAY: "All Jews did ritual ablution. Mikvaot are everywhere."
(@ 127:45)

One line, and it broke Abke's exclusivity claim 28 minutes after he made it. The immersion distinctive is not unique; the CLUSTER is what is unusual.

Say density and cluster. Never say "only" or "nowhere else".

THE STRATEGIC PROBLEM, not an objection.
(@ 52:21, 70:04, 70:34)

Huff and Boyce BOTH pre-emptively disowned faith-alone ticket-punching: "that's mega-church stuff, post-1960s; Rome doesn't teach it, Orthodoxy doesn't, Anglicans don't, Lutherans don't."

Several of our strongest cards are built to attack a position neither opponent holds. Against a liturgical opponent, the blood-atonement card swings at air. Know that before you lead with it.

BOYCE WILL SAY: "John 14:26 licenses the non-red letters."
(@ 61:16-63:52)

Jesus — in the red text — promises the Paraclete so the apostles would not merely remember his words but UNDERSTAND them. So the apostolic interpretation is authorised by Jesus himself, and red-letters-only is unbiblical on its own terms.

The best unanswered methodological objection in ten hours of debate. Zero hits for John 14:26 anywhere in questions/. Expect it. Have something.

JONES WILL SAY: Acts 10 — "rise, kill and eat" — and he will point out the author tells it TWICE.
("Was Jesus Actually a Vegan?" @ 28:36, 30:01, 34:51)

"How many times does that author put the same story in twice?"

This is his most-used text and it is NOWHERE on our card. Kam's answer — "it says a voice, not God" — fails on Acts 10:14, where Peter answers "Not so, LORD." Jones pressed exactly that and Kam would not answer yes or no.

The defensible line: the vision's own stated meaning is Gentile inclusion (10:28, 10:34-35), which Jones CONCEDED @ 33:18. Take the concession; do not fight the lexicon.

Acts 10:13-14 (KJV) — "And there came a voice to him, Rise, Peter; kill, and eat. But Peter said, Not so, Lord; for I have never eaten any thing that is common or unclean."

JONES WILL SAY: Genesis 8:20-21 — God smells Noah's burnt offering and calls it good.
(@ 42:50)

"The sacrificial system of Israel was founded upon that sacrifice."

God's explicit approval of animal sacrifice at the narrative reset. Not on our card in any form. Harder than Leviticus, because it is approval rather than legislation.

JONES WILL SAY: Genesis 9:3 is the NOAHIC covenant — the one we live under. The Adamic one ended.
(@ 47:48)

A clean structural answer to Genesis 1:29 that Kam never dismantled. It does not deny 1:29; it dates it.

Genesis 9:3 (KJV) — "Every moving thing that liveth shall be meat for you; even as the green herb have I given you all things."

THE ANSWER IS MATTHEW 19:8 (see the starred frame). Jesus treats a standing Mosaic permission as a concession and appeals past it to the beginning. That is exactly the move this objection needs, in his own voice.

JONES WILL SAY: Deuteronomy 14:3-5 — and "there are 635 laws in Torah and not one says you may not eat meat."
(@ 48:30, 153:44)

Deuteronomy 14:4-5 (KJV) — "These are the beasts which ye shall eat: the ox, the sheep, and the goat, the hart, and the roebuck, and the fallow deer..."

True, and it does not touch claim A as properly stated. Our claim is about a SECT'S practice and a prophetic critique of the cult, not about a Torah prohibition. Agreeing here costs nothing.

JONES WILL SAY: the Damascus Document legislates eating locusts and fish. CD 12:11-15.
(@ 59:20)

"Locusts thrown alive into fire or boiling water; fish cut open alive to drain the blood. These do not seem like animal liberationists."

His most damaging TECHNICAL argument, substantially accurate — and CD 12 is NOT in our Dead Sea Scrolls selection. We cannot currently check it. Acquire it before anyone argues the Essene menu again.

JONES WILL SAY: John 21 — Jesus COMMANDED the catch.
(@ 69:06, 103:34, 104:40)

Not merely "he ate fish" but "he performed a miracle to fill the net, then cooked it." Asked three times. Kam called it "a great question" and never answered.

And his closer, which is the best line either opponent produced all night:
"Pythagoras let the fish go but Jesus didn't. That's the point of the story — I'm not Pythagoras, I'm Jesus, we eat fish."

Distinct from Luke 24 and sharper. Prepare it separately.

JONES WILL SAY: "We can't get behind the text. All we've got is the text."
(@ 98:00) — "the first thing they teach you in seminary."

And: "Conversion does not give you hermeneutical authority over the Bible." (@ 123:42)

This frame pre-defeats most reconstruction arguments before they start. Plus the credential move (@ 10:53, 151:50): "I don't want to pull rank but I've got a PhD."

No counter-frame exists anywhere in the repo.

JONES WILL SAY: the gospel writers used the LXX, not the Hebrew.
(@ 164:55)

Both halves of the Temple quotation are verbatim LXX; the Greek is spelaion leston, "cave of bandits", identical in Mark, Matthew and Luke; and Jeremiah 7:9, two verses earlier, already has thieves and murderers in the ordinary human sense.

This single move answers a whole FAMILY of our Hebrew-lexical arguments at once — paritz, shachat, thuo. Total gap on the card.

JONES ALSO RUNS: the gnosticism frame (@ 56:28 and eight more times), the argument from silence as a named category (@ 21:43), and "the early-church debate was about eidolothyta — meat sacrificed to Roman gods — not about meat" (@ 19:53).

Note for your own confidence: he argued the idol-meat thesis for ten minutes and never once cited 1 Corinthians 8:8 or 10:25, the chapters that contain it. He is beatable on his own ground. He is not beatable on the apparatus.

HOLE 5 — NEW, AND THE WORST ONE. Isaiah 25:6.

"And in this mountain shall the LORD of hosts make unto all people a feast of fat things... of fat things full of marrow, of wines on the lees well refined."

THE SAME HOLY MOUNTAIN as Isaiah 11:9 ("they shall not hurt nor destroy") and Isaiah 56:7 ("my holy mountain... house of prayer"). Fourteen chapters later. Same prophet.

An eschatological MEAT-AND-WINE BANQUET sitting underneath the entire peaceable-kingdom architecture. Jones raised it in one interrupted sentence (@ 120:22), was cut off with "whoa whoa friend", and took the point anyway.

It appears nowhere in this repo in any form. If you build on Isaiah 11, you must own Isaiah 25 first.

WHY SIX VERSES ON THIS BOARD ARE QUOTED IN NOTES INSTEAD OF SHOWN AS VERSE CARDS

The Desk can only lay out a verse that some card's prose already points at — that is how the build guarantees a verse card is real. These six are not referenced by any card yet:

Isaiah 25:6 · Matthew 19:8 · Acts 10:13-15 · Genesis 9:3 · Deuteronomy 14:3-5 · Mark 11:18

All six are in the held KJV and were checked there by hand. Each is quoted in the note beside its argument.

To promote them to real verse cards — with the reader pane and the HELD stamp — each needs one line of prose on a card. That is a content change to public pages, so it is Matt's and Rex's call, not something this board should do quietly.

Worth doing. Four of the six are the counter-texts our own audit says the sacrifice card is missing.

HOLE 1 — Acts 21:23-26. James tells Paul to pay for four men's Temple offerings, and Paul does it.

Our single highest-threat text, because it is the James household itself participating in the sacrificial system.

Worth knowing: in three hours Jones NEVER RAISED IT. He used the cheaper Acts 3:1 (the disciples going up to the Temple at the hour of prayer) and said he had spent the week researching James. Our worst problem is apparently not in the standard opponent's kit. Do not volunteer it.

HOLE 2 — Isaiah 56:7, first half: "their burnt offerings and their sacrifices shall be accepted upon mine altar."

We quote the second half. The first half is pro-sacrifice, in the same verse.

DO NOT say the clause is "a known interpolation". No scholar is named and there is no source. Kam said exactly that on camera (@ 123:08) and got away with it only because Jones never read the first half aloud.

HOLE 3 — Thomas 14 and Q 10:8 / Luke 10:8: "eat such things as are set before you."

Jesus instructing his own itinerants not to be fussy about food, in two of our own top-tier sources.

Neither side mentioned the Gospel of Thomas ONCE in 41,000 words. Source #2 in our hierarchy, absent from the biggest debate on the question. That cuts both ways: nobody has used Thomas 12 against us either.

HOLE 4 — the James-household inference.

Hegesippus on James's diet comes through Eusebius, is late, and is hagiography. Jones: "this idea that James the Just was a vegetarian is in, like, two obscure sources" (@ 39:33).

The answer he never got is the chain-of-custody paragraph on the card. It was available and was not said.

HOLE 6 — Luke 2:24. The holy family brings two turtledoves to the Temple.
(Huff/Boyce debate, trailer @ 00:28 — so it is almost certainly in part 2)

"Was Jesus's parents, who apparently were part of the Essene group of some sort, wrong for bringing these doves to the temple?"

HARDER THAN ACTS 21, because it is his own parents, in the infancy narrative, with no plausible distance. Zero hits for Luke 2:24 in questions/.

FIVE OF THE ITEMS IN THIS FRAME WERE SAID ON CAMERA BY OUR OWN SIDE.

Two were destroyed on the recording. Three survived only because the opponent did not know them.

This list is not hygiene. It is a record of how this argument loses in public. Every line below is checkable by a hostile viewer in under a minute.

X "Qumran was anti-sacrifice."
The Temple Scroll prescribes it and 4QMMT is about doing it CORRECTLY. Boycott of a corrupt priesthood, not abolition of sacrifice.

X "Porphyry says the Essenes abstained from all animal food."
He does not; the line is not in his text. Nor do Philo, Josephus or Pliny say it. Only Jerome (393) does — and he credits Josephus, who does not.

X "Isaiah 11:9's destroy is the word for ritual slaughter."
FALSE. Isaiah 11:9 is shachath (ruin). Ritual slaughter is shachat, final tet. Different roots, identical only in loose transliteration.

Deleted from the repo as false on 2026-10-06 — and then said on THREE separate recordings anyway. Huff reads Hebrew. A lexicon ends this in ten seconds.

X "Luke 24:42 is textually unstable."
DESTROYED ON CAMERA. Jones produced a Greek New Testament and read the apparatus: every manuscript has fish; NONE has honeycomb alone. Only the honeycomb is a variant. Then: "commentaries are not manuscripts."

Concede the verse. It costs almost nothing and defending it costs the room.

X The 153 fish / Pythagoras argument.
DESTROYED ON CAMERA, in three moves: no evidence any Galilean knew Pythagorean literature; the ICHTHYS acrostic post-dates the gospels; and "Pythagoras let the fish go but Jesus didn't."

Retire it completely.

X Hosea's "not" is lo, which means "never, not a comparison."
The parallel line in Hosea 6:6b uses the comparative min. Said FOUR times on one recording and survived only by luck.

The verse is strong without this. Quote it and stop.

X "The Nazarene sect was before Christ" — Epiphanius.
FABRICATED. No section number, no Panarion in this repo; traced to an auto-caption of podcast episode 026. It has since appeared on a SLIDE, in quotation marks, in a public debate.

Related: Panarion 18 (Nasaraeans) and Panarion 29 (Nazoraeans) are different entries. Four of our files conflate them and use the same passage to prove opposite things.

X "I have no desire to eat the flesh of this Passover" as Jesus's words.
It is Epiphanius quoting the EBIONITES' version of Luke 22:15, presented by him as their alteration — a negated wordplay on the Greek. Evidence of what that movement believed. Not evidence of what Jesus said.

X Three lexical errors added to the list this month:

ethnos does NOT mean "herds and flocks" (it means nation; flock is poimne).

"Humane" is not the root of "human" — they are doublets of the same Latin word.

The hiphil IS the causative stem; saying it "doesn't necessarily mean caused" inverts it.

Four of our recurring errors are lexical. A public-domain lexicon would end all of them permanently.

X Any Dr. Tabor quotation taken from a transcript, podcast or course.
All Tabor material in this repo is auto-caption. Attribute his POSITIONS by paraphrase from his published books. Never put quotation marks around him.

X The Essene Gospel of Peace as an ancient text. It is Szekely, twentieth century.

STRONGER ARGUMENTS, FOUND 2026-10-16

Three agents read all twelve of Kam's guest appearances — about 22 hours — against this card and the mining report, asked one question: is anything here STRONGER than what we lead with?

Honest headline: nothing beats the Recognitions block for claim A, and nothing in 22 hours is stronger for claim B. But SIX things are stronger at specific pressure points, and two of those points currently have no answer at all.

Two of the six are already in this repo, held verbatim, used nowhere.

4. EZEKIEL 20:25-26 — a canonical warrant for the concession theory

"Wherefore I gave them also statutes that were not good, and judgments whereby they should not live" — and v. 26 illustrates it with an OFFERING practice.

Better than Matthew 19:8 on subject matter: the not-good statute is about offerings, not divorce. Prophetic, canonical, and it pre-empts the classical-theism objection ("God cannot command what is immoral") from inside the canon instead of from philosophy.

Held in our KJV. Present in only one research file; absent from every card.

Concede first: the mainstream reading of v.26 is judicial abandonment to Molech practice. The narrow form is all you need — the canon itself says God can give statutes that are not good, and the example it reaches for is an offering.

★ 1. THE GENESIS APOCRYPHON (1QapGen XI)
Tabor reads it aloud on air — kam-guest-08 @ 42:41:

"Do not fear, Noah... I give all of it to you and to your sons to eat the green things and the grass of the earth, but you shall not eat any blood."

A pre-Christian Hebrew/Aramaic manuscript whose version of Noah's post-flood grant has NO FLESH PERMISSION.

This answers Genesis 9:3 — the single most-used counter-text in every one of these debates, and a hole with no answer on the card. Tabor called it "quite remarkable" and volunteered that he had "never read it with this in mind."

NOT HELD. Zero hits in the repo. Cave 1, not Cave 4 — Tabor corrected Kam on that live. Highest-value acquisition from the twelve.

5. JEREMIAH 7:21 — the clause we have been leaving out

The card quotes 7:22. Read 7:21 first:

"Put your burnt offerings unto your sacrifices, AND EAT FLESH."

The sarcastic permission names eating the flesh, not just the altar. It welds the diet half to the sacrifice half inside the verse the card already leads with, in the Masoretic text, with no appeal to a versional variant.

Kam reached for an unverifiable Syriac Peshitta reading of 7:22 instead (kam-guest-01 @ 128:09). He did not need it. Reaching for an unheld variant when the received text already carries the point is exactly how the Luke 24:42 exchange was lost.

★ 2. IRENAEUS, AGAINST HERESIES 5.33.3-4
(kam-guest-06 @ 64:46, read on air by the host)

"...it is right that when the creation is restored, all the animals should obey and be in subjection to man and revert to the food originally given by God... that is, the productions of the earth."

A hostile orthodox father, c. 180, who CONDEMNS the Ebionites elsewhere — reading Isaiah 11 exactly the way we do. That is the hostile-witness structure this card says is its strongest form, applied to the Eden-to-Kingdom frame the mining report called "upstream of everything."

NOT HELD, zero hits — and the ANF translation is PUBLIC DOMAIN, so this one is free to add today. Cite it as Book 5, ch. 33, §§3-4; Kam gives the numbers wrongly three times and the host catches it on air.

6. TWO SMALLER UPGRADES

LEVITICUS 5:11-13 — a bloodless flour sin offering, with atonement explicitly granted, INSIDE the priestly source. Tabor calls it "quite the anomaly." Zero hits in the repo. Limit: it is a concession for the poor, so it proves the blood requirement is not absolute — not that it was never commanded.

LUKE 7:33 NAMES BREAD — so the "eating and drinking" of Q 7:34 takes bread and wine as its antecedents. This upgrades HOLE 3 from a rhetorical answer ("a quotation of an insult, not a menu") to a textual one, and it is Tabor's own argument, made twice. Caveat: it concedes the wine outright, which is what broke HOLE 4.

Also: Proverbs 23:20 — "riotous eaters of flesh" — gives the Q 7:34 slur a primary text. The pairing flesh-eater + wine-drinker is proverbial, so the critics reached for a stock formula.

★ 3. WE ALREADY HOLD THIS AND HAVE NEVER USED IT
1 Enoch 7:5 + Clementine Homilies 8.16-8.17.

The card quotes Hom. 8.15 and stops. It never says what chapter 8.15 is: it is titled "The Giants", and the NEXT chapter is titled "Cannibalism". The Clementine argument IS the Enochic argument, and the card quotes the conclusion while dropping the premise.

Hom. 8.16 — "it was not a long step to the consumption of flesh like their own, having first tasted it in other forms."
Hom. 8.17 — "by the shedding of much blood, the pure air being defiled" — the flood as a purgation of bloodshed.

Together they answer Genesis 9:3, Genesis 8:20-21 AND the no-death-free-meal flank — three of the mining report's new holes — because 8.15 makes NECESSITY the hinge and 8.16 makes the objection INTENTIONAL killing.

Both Tier 1. Both verified verbatim this session. Zero hits for Enoch or the Watchers anywhere in questions/.

THE HARD NEWS, AND IT IS IMPORTANT

1. THE ISAIAH 11:9 ERROR ORIGINATES WITH TABOR. He states on air (kam-guest-08 @ 11:53, 28:36) that "destroy" is shachat, slaughter — and Kam says Tabor gave him that in the Christspiracy interview. So the repo's banned lexical error came from our own best scholar.

The ban holds anyway: anyone with a lexicon refutes it and Huff reads Hebrew. But do not expect Tabor to supply cover, and do not cite him for it. The honest version is available — Genesis 6:11's "corrupt" IS shachath, so the Isaiah 11:9 / Genesis 6:11 verbal link is real. It is the shechitah link that is false.

2. THE ISAIAH 56:7 "INTERPOLATION" LOOKS LIKE A TRANSFERRED ARGUMENT. Kam now attributes it to Tabor by name (kam-guest-07 @ 51:34) — but in the recording where Tabor is actually present, Tabor makes that argument about PSALM 51:18-19, not Isaiah 56.

And the legitimate Psalm 51 version is ALREADY IN THIS REPO, on the blood-atonement card, verified against our KJV. One edit removes a fabricated citation, replaces it with a defensible one, and explains where the fabrication came from. Cleanest fix available.

THE BEST UNANSWERED OBJECTION IN THE TWELVE
kam-guest-09 @ 88:46, from a Greek Orthodox theologian:

"Epistemologically, your Hebrew Gospel argument has heavy dependence on the church fathers. Why would the fathers who mention the longer ending of Mark 16 not be authoritative, but when they mention the Gospel of Matthew, it is?"

Kam answered with the criterion of embarrassment, which is a category error: embarrassment vouches for a hostile witness reporting content against his own interest. It says nothing about whether the father correctly IDENTIFIED the text — which is the actual question. And Mark 16 is attested by the same fathers.

He then cited an unpublished private document and ran out of time.

THE REPO HAS NO ANSWER TO THIS ANYWHERE. Expect it from any trained opponent.

THREE THINGS TO STOP SAYING, ADDED THIS MONTH

X GENESIS 9:3's "every moving thing" = remes = "BUGS".
Refuted by our own KJV twice over: Gen 9:2 already enumerates beast, fowl and fish and says "into your hand are they delivered"; and Psalm 104:25 uses the same word of SEA CREATURES. Currently load-bearing, said on at least three recordings, and unchallenged. The Genesis Apocryphon makes it completely unnecessary.

X "DOMINION" = yarad, "to lower oneself in service".
Genesis 1:26 is the regular qal of radah, "to rule." Kam explicitly denies radah is the root. This is the shachath error again, in the load-bearing verse of the whole Genesis argument. The stewardship point stands without the etymology.

X THE GENESIS APOCRYPHON AS "AN EARLIER READING BY DEFAULT" (kam-guest-10 @ 26:03).
It is rewritten Bible, not a Genesis manuscript — so it is not a textual witness to Gen 9:3 at all. Use it as a PARALLEL TRADITION, which is strong, not as a variant, which is false in kind.

IN THE DISTRIBUTED FILM — so discipline alone cannot fix these

"Josephus tells you that John the Baptist lived only stems, roots, and fruits" (kam-guest-12 @ 30:00, and in the narration).
JOSEPHUS SAYS NOTHING ABOUT JOHN'S DIET. "Stems, roots and fruits" is Josephus on BANNUS, his own desert teacher (Life 2.11) — a different person. An opponent with Josephus open ends the segment.

"When Epiphanius talked to one of the Nazarenes personally, the Nazarene said: 'Because Jesus taught us to be vegetarians'" (kam-guest-12 @ 32:27, in quotation marks, in the film).
NO SUCH INTERVIEW EXISTS IN THE PANARION. This has the exact profile of the fabrications already catalogued — a quotation mark acquired around a paraphrase. Treat as suspected fabrication and verify before it is repeated.

The 153-fish / Pythagoras block is also in the film, after being destroyed on camera. The repo should hold a written correction for all three.

BANK THESE. A credentialed opponent said them on the record.

Rev. Tony Jones, PhD, @ 121:26:
"We have no idea if the early Christians before the temple came down still participated in Jewish animal sacrifice. We don't know. I think a lot of us think they probably didn't, which is good."

Jones @ 122:20: agreement that essentially every animal eaten in that world, in Rome or Israel, was ritually slaughtered first.

The first concedes that the sacrifice half of claim A is OPEN — from the opposition. The second collapses the distance between "sacrifice" and "meat" in antiquity, which is the hinge of the whole argument.

Neither was captured in the moment. Capture them.

ALSO BANKABLE:

Boyce volunteered his own fringe status to de-weaponise the word "fringe" — and he holds a HEBREW-MATTHEW position himself. An overlap our side never exploited.

Ray Hicks (carnivore) conceded: humans are not carnivores, meat is not necessary, Eden was plant-prescribed, Eden is the ideal, "I'm a hypocrite", "I definitely have moral inconsistencies."

And then did not move. Which is its own lesson: winning the exegesis is not what moves anyone.

WE HOLD ALL OF THIS AND NOBODY USED ANY OF IT.

In a three-hour debate Jones said "I never hear you quote the Didache" — and then got the Didache BACKWARDS, claiming it permits food offered to idols.

Didache 6:3, in our own Tier 1 file: "keep strictly away from what is offered to idols, for that implies worshiping dead gods."

The biggest unexploited rebuttal in ten hours, sitting in a file we already hold.

The Clementines were never mentioned ONCE in ten hours.

Kam said "Peter clearly ate only plants and I can give you multiple instances" (@ 37:04) and then gave none — while Homilies 12.6 sits in this repo, verbatim: "I use only bread and olives, and rarely pot-herbs."

And Recognitions 1.39 is titled "Baptism Instituted in Place of Sacrifices" — exactly the argument he made from nothing at @ 107:50.

Romans 14:2 — "another, who is weak, eateth herbs."

Paul, c. 57 CE, conceding the existence of vegetable-only believers AGAINST his own argument, in a debate about whether early Christian vegetarians existed.

Unused. It is the best single witness for claim A and it is thirty years earlier than anything else in the stack.

Eusebius, Demonstratio Evangelica 1.10, read on air by Abke (@ 102:37): "he did not enjoin sacrifices or require them... nor did he lay down any other of the various precepts of Moses except the spiritual laws."

The repo holds DE 3.5 only. 1.10 is STRONGER for this card and is not held. Get it.

THE SENTENCE THAT HOLDS EVERY WORD

The movement that claimed succession from Jesus through his brother James rejected sacrifice and abstained from flesh — and we know it from the people who were trying to discredit it.

That sentence is defensible all night. Everything stronger than it is a liability.

4. Panarion 18 / 29 / 30 in usable excerpts.
